title: When the Playlist Burns
premise: Casper Zhou, seventeen, has spent three years keeping his family afloat while his mother works hospital night shifts, and he's perfected the art of being unremarkable at Meridian High. When a college essay prompt demands the story he's never told, he starts writing about the fire that gutted the music wing two years ago—a fire the school board called an accident, but which Casper slowly realizes was arson covered up to protect a beloved teacher and a donor's reputation. Digging in with his best friend Priya and his little sister Junie's stolen recordings, Casper uncovers that the burned wing was scheduled for demolition anyway, that insurance money vanished into the superintendent's pet project, and that the one witness—a deaf percussionist named Theo—was quietly pushed out of the district. As the final audition for the rebuilt arts program approaches, Casper must choose between the scholarship that depends on staying quiet and the justice Theo never got. He publishes everything during the audition itself, sacrificing his own clean record, and ends the book testifying at a state hearing—not as the invisible caretaker, but as the eldest Zhou kid who finally stopped being fine.
about_author: Odile Thornbury is a former debate coach who grew up translating paperwork for her immigrant parents in a rust-belt town much like Meridian. She writes stories about kids who hold families together and then have to learn to hold themselves.

chapters.title: Everything Is Fine
chapters.summary: POV Casper. A chaotic morning—burnt toast, Junie's lost clarinet reeds, mom's night-shift exhaustion—and Casper smooths it all over before school. At Meridian, he's the reliable nobody. The emotional beat: competent exhaustion disguised as calm, establishing what 'fine' costs him.

chapters.title: The Prompt
chapters.summary: POV Casper. English class receives the college essay prompt: 'Tell us about a moment you couldn't take back.' Casper freezes when his mind goes straight to the music-wing fire. His draft comes out angry and true, shocking even him. Beat: the first crack in the armor; honesty feels dangerous.

chapters.title: Ash Wednesday, Two Years Gone
chapters.summary: POV Casper, flashback braided with present. He revisits the night of the fire—the orange glow, the crowd, Mr. Voss the choir teacher weeping on the curb. Official story: faulty wiring. But Casper remembers the smell of accelerant and the security guard who was suddenly reassigned. Beat: memory refuses to stay buried.

chapters.title: Junie's Recordings
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Cleaning the shared laptop, he finds Junie's audio files: she'd been recording practice sessions in the wing the week of the fire, and one file captures voices arguing after hours. Beat: dread mixed with electric purpose—the past hands him evidence.

chapters.title: Priya Doesn't Believe Him (Yet)
chapters.summary: POV Priya. Casper drags his best friend into the library with headphones. She hears footsteps, a man saying 'the board signed off,' and goes from skeptic to co-conspirator in one lunch period. Beat: alliance formed; the burden halves and doubles at once.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Left
chapters.summary: POV Casper. He tracks down Theo Nakamura, the deaf percussionist who was in the building that night and transferred out within a month. Theo agrees to meet but is guarded, communicating through a text thread. Beat: guilt surfaces—Casper realizes others paid for his silence too.

chapters.title: What Theo Saw
chapters.summary: POV Theo. Through sign via video call and typed messages, Theo describes seeing Assistant Superintendent Dale Harrow leaving the wing minutes before flames, and how adults told him his 'misunderstanding' would ruin his college chances. Beat: righteous anger; the cover-up had a human casualty.

chapters.title: Essay Due, Life Interrupted
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Mom picks up extra shifts when the furnace dies; Casper abandons the essay mid-draft to handle rent panic and babysitting. Ms. Okafor, his English teacher, gives him an extension and one line: 'Write the thing you're afraid of.' Beat: the cost of caring for everyone but himself.

chapters.title: Board Minutes and Redactions
chapters.summary: POV Priya. A records request through the public library yields board meeting minutes with suspicious redactions: the wing was slated for demolition, insurance payout $1.2M, routed to the Harrow Athletic Complex. Beat: the conspiracy takes shape on paper.

chapters.title: Mr. Voss Breaks
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Casper confronts Voss gently at the rebuilt program's fundraiser. Voss admits he suspected arson but was threatened with termination and his students' college recommendations. He begs Casper to let it go. Beat: moral complexity—the first victim is also a collaborator.

chapters.title: Threats, Softly Delivered
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Harrow corners Casper after class with a smile and a warning about 'unstable home situations' affecting scholarship review. That night someone keys the word LIAR into Casper's locker. Beat: fear arrives; the stakes turn personal and physical.

chapters.title: Mom Finds Out
chapters.summary: POV Mom (brief) then Casper. Mom discovers the locker damage and the investigation notebook under Casper's bed. Instead of forbidding him, she tells him about every complaint she filed at the hospital that went nowhere. Beat: intergenerational solidarity; silence inherited and refused.

chapters.title: The Audition Stakes
chapters.summary: POV Casper. The final audition for the new arts conservatory track doubles as Casper's scholarship shot—he's accompanying Junie's clarinet piece. Winning means tuition help; publishing means disqualification risk. Beat: the trap closes; both paths cost something irreplaceable.

chapters.title: Hacking the Paper Trail
chapters.summary: POV Priya. Priya cross-references the contractor's invoices with Harrow's brother-in-law's company—same address, same shell. Theo sends a photo he took that night: Harrow's car in the loading zone, timestamped eleven minutes before the alarm. Beat: triumph before the fall; the case is nearly airtight.

chapters.title: Voss Recants
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Pressured again by the district, Voss publicly calls Casper's claims 'a grieving student's fantasy' in the school paper. Casper's allies waver; Junie overhears classmates mocking her brother. Beat: betrayal and isolation—the lowest point begins.

chapters.title: Junie's File Goes Missing
chapters.summary: POV Casper. The original recording vanishes from the laptop; a break-in ransacks their apartment but takes only electronics. Casper realizes he kept a backup on a burned CD in Junie's clarinet case all along. Beat: despair pivoting to defiance—the family's smallness becomes its armor.

chapters.title: The Choice
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Night before auditions, Casper drafts the exposé with Priya and Theo: names, documents, timestamps. Publishing means losing the scholarship, maybe graduation privileges, maybe worse. Mom says, 'We've survived worse than being right.' Beat: resolve crystallizes.

chapters.title: Final Audition
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Junie performs beautifully; Casper accompanies her with shaking hands, knowing what happens next. As Harrow takes the stage to announce the conservatory cohort, Casper walks to the podium instead. Beat: held breath—the calm before detonation.

chapters.title: When the Playlist Burns
chapters.summary: POV multiple, rapid cuts. Casper plays Junie's recovered recording over the auditorium speakers—the argument, 'the board signed off'—while Priya live-publishes the full dossier. Chaos, then Theo signs to the room: 'I saw him.' Harrow's face collapses. Beat: cathartic climax; truth made undeniable and public.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Loud and Quiet
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Harrow suspended pending criminal charges; Voss resigns and finally apologizes to Theo. The district threatens Casper's transcript; local press turns him into a symbol he didn't ask to be. Beat: victory with bruises—justice is messy, not cinematic.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: POV Casper. At the state education hearing, Casper testifies alongside Theo and Mom. He reads aloud the college essay he finally finished—about the fire, the silence, and choosing to be heard. Beat: identity reclaimed; the boy who raised everyone stands up for himself.

chapters.title: Encore
chapters.summary: POV Casper, epilogue. Months later: the conservatory offers Junie a place, an anonymous donor funds Theo's return, and Casper gets an acceptance letter from a college that loved the essay exactly as it was. On the porch with his siblings, he updates the family playlist. Beat: warm resolution—no longer invisible, no longer alone.
